title.vi: Từ làm thay đổi đáp án

prefer.def: To like one thing more than another thing.
prefer.ex: I *prefer* the park to the beach because it's quieter.

favourite part.def: The bit of something that you like the most.
favourite part.ex: My *favourite part* of the trip was the boat ride.

recommend.def: To tell someone that something is good and they should try it.
recommend.ex: I *recommend* the new climbing wall. It's great fun!

disappointed.def: Sad because something was not as good as you hoped.
disappointed.ex: We were *disappointed* because the match was cancelled.

I'm not keen on.def: A polite way to say you don't like something very much.
I'm not keen on.ex: *I'm not keen on* spicy food, so I chose the soup.

actually.def: Used to give the true fact, often when it is different from what someone thought.
actually.ex: I thought it started at six, but *actually* it starts at seven.

instead.def: In the place of something else.
instead.ex: It was raining, so we played board games *instead*.

although.def: Used to join two ideas that seem different.
although.ex: *Although* the walk was long, I really enjoyed it.

in the end.def: What finally happened, after thinking or after some changes.
in the end.ex: We wanted pizza, but *in the end* we had noodles.

it's worth it.def: Something is good enough to spend your time, money or effort on.
it's worth it.ex: The climb is hard, but *it's worth it* for the view.

find out.def: To learn a fact or some news.
find out.ex: How did you *find out* about the chess club?

reason.def: Why something happens or why someone does something.
reason.ex: The *reason* she joined the club is that her best friend is in it.

mention.def: To say something quickly, without talking about it a lot.
mention.ex: He *mentioned* the museum, but he didn't go there.

whys: Reza was going to take the bus, but it leaves really early, so he changed his plan.

Noah wanted to go home earlier, but his feelings changed by the end.

whys: Sports day was going to be on Friday, but the field is too wet.
Thursday afternoon is the prize-giving, not sports day.
v.hint: The question says *now*, so the plan has changed. Listen for the new day, not the old one.

whys: 1998 is when Grandpa got his phone, not Grandma.
2004 is when Grandma bought her first computer, not her phone.
v.hint: Three years are said. Listen for who got what, and match each year to the right person and thing.
v.worked: Grandma says "*I got mine in 2003*".

stim.head: Listen to Adam and his grandma.
lines: Grandma, when did you get your first mobile phone?
Let me think. Your grandpa got one in 1998, but I didn't want one then. I got mine in 2003, when your mum started university. And I bought my first computer in 2004.

v.q: How long did Lucy's walk to the library take yesterday?
whys: Ten minutes is what the sign says, but Lucy's walk took longer.
Five minutes is how long it takes by bike, not on foot.
v.hint: Several times are said. The question says *yesterday*, so listen for the time that goes with that word.
v.worked: Lucy says "*it took me twenty-five yesterday*" because she stopped at the shops.

stim.head: Listen to Lucy and her dad.
lines: How long does it take to walk to the new library, Lucy?
The sign says ten minutes, but it took me twenty-five yesterday because I stopped to look in the shops! By bike it's only five minutes.

whys: Six years is how long Khoa's sister has played.
Half an hour is how long Khoa practises every day.
v.hint: The question asks *how long*. Listen for *for* and a length of time, and check who it is about.
v.worked: Khoa says "*For three years* now".

stim.head: Listen to Khoa and his teacher.
lines: Khoa, how long have you played the violin?
For three years now. I started when I was seven. My sister has played for six years, so she's much better than me! I practise for half an hour every day.

It was better than the penguin film.

Nora says the pictures were beautiful, and it was the end that was boring.
v.hint: Nora says good and bad things. Listen for *But* and *actually*, because they often bring the speaker's real opinion.
v.worked: Nora says "*the film was really long*" and the end was boring.

lines: What did you think of the film about whales, Nora?
The pictures of the whales were beautiful. But the film was really long, and actually, I found the end quite boring. I preferred the one about penguins last week.
Really? I thought the penguin one was boring!

lines: Do you like the new school timetable, Ali?
Not really. I'm not keen on having maths straight after lunch, because I always feel sleepy. Starting at eight is fine, though, and I love having PE on Mondays.
Well, maybe have a smaller lunch!

opts: to swim safely in the sea
whys: Amira says her friends are "not the reason".
Amira says it's not to get fit, because she already plays basketball.
v.hint: The question asks *why*. Listen for *not*, which tells you which ideas to cross out.
v.worked: Amira says she wants "to *swim in the waves safely*" when she stays by the sea.

stim.head: Listen to Amira and her grandpa.
lines: Why do you want to learn to swim, Amira? Is it because your friends can?
Some of my friends can, but that's not the reason. We're going to stay by the sea in the summer, and I want to swim in the waves safely. It's not to get fit, either. I already play basketball.

whys: Luca says the guitar wasn't too hard.
Luca says his teacher was great.
v.hint: The question asks *why*. Speakers often say what was fine first, so listen for the real reason after *But*.
v.worked: The lessons were on Saturday mornings, and "*that's when my football team plays*".

lines: Luca, why did you give up the guitar? You were really good!
Thanks! It wasn't too hard, and my teacher was great. But the lessons were on Saturday mornings, and that's when my football team plays. I'm going to try the piano instead.

whys: Jack says the campfire was fun, but it was not the best bit.
Jack says the night walk was a bit scary, but it was not the best bit.
v.hint: The question says *favourite*, but speakers may use other words. Listen for a phrase that means the same, often after *But*.
v.worked: Jack says "*the best bit was the canoeing*".

stim.head: Listen to Jack and his uncle.
lines: So, Jack, what was your favourite part of the school camp?
The campfire was fun, and the night walk was a bit scary. But the best bit was the canoeing. We raced the teachers across the lake, and we won!

whys: Hana says feeding the goats was sweet, but it was not her favourite.
Hana says the tractor ride was only OK.
v.hint: Hana talks about three activities. Listen for a word that matches *like best* in the question.
v.worked: Hana says "*milking the cow was my favourite*".

stim.head: Listen to Hana and her dad.
lines: Which part of the farm visit did you like best, Hana?
Feeding the baby goats was sweet, and the tractor ride was OK. But milking the cow was my favourite. It was harder than I expected, but really funny!
Ha! I'd like to see you try that again.

items.en: In Part 3, all three options are usually *said* in the talk. Don't choose an option just because you hear it.
items.vi: Ở Phần 3, cả ba lựa chọn thường đều được *nói* trong bài. Đừng chọn chỉ vì em nghe thấy từ đó.
example: Question: Which club did Ruby join? (drama / art / chess)
Ruby: I looked at drama and art, but *in the end* I joined the *chess* club.

items.en: Listen for words that *change* the answer: *but*, *actually*, *instead*, *in the end*.
items.vi: Hãy nghe những từ *thay đổi* đáp án: *but*, *actually*, *instead*, *in the end*.
example: I was going to take the bus, *but* I went by car *instead*.
I thought it was on Friday. *Actually*, it's on Wednesday.

items.en: Learn the opinion words: *prefer*, *favourite part*, *I'm not keen on*, *disappointed*, *recommend*.
items.vi: Học các từ chỉ ý kiến: *prefer*, *favourite part*, *I'm not keen on*, *disappointed*, *recommend*.
example: *The best bit* was the canoeing. (= my favourite part)
*I'm not keen on* fish. (= I don't like it much)

items.en: The *reason* often comes after *because*, or before *so*.
items.vi: *Lý do* thường đứng sau *because*, hoặc đứng trước *so*.
example: I chose a goldfish *because* I can watch it after school.
It's free for children, *so* it's worth it.

items.en: The options use *different words* from the talk. Match the *meaning*, not the word.
items.vi: Các lựa chọn dùng *từ khác* với bài nghe. Hãy chọn theo *ý nghĩa*, không theo từ.
example: Talk: *It was worth it.* Option: *He's glad he did it.*
Talk: *It cost a lot.* Option: *It was expensive.*

items.en: The questions follow the *order* of the talk. Read them first and decide what to listen for.
items.vi: Các câu hỏi đi theo *thứ tự* của bài nghe. Hãy đọc trước và xác định cần nghe gì.
example: *How long*...? Listen for minutes, weeks or years.
